threatModelSummary: This feature adds filesDeleted/testFilesDeleted claim fields to loom's own pipeline-state schemas, a second claim direction (MustNotExist) to PathClaim, and a requireNoRenameArrows validation rule — all inside loom's own orchestrator/state packages that validate an agent's self-reported work against the filesystem and git-observed changes. There is no user-facing input, no auth, no network call, no secret handling, and no new dependency (go.mod/go.sum unchanged, confirmed via diff). The spec's own Trust Boundaries section states 'None — paths are checked inside the run's own worktree only,' and the implementation does not cross that: resolveWithinRoot (pre-existing, unmodified by this change) still clamps every claimed path to the project root before any stat, so the new deletion-claim path (existingPaths/missingPaths) inherits the same traversal guard as the existing existence-claim path. The only functional diff in this iteration was a doc-comment fix on posture.go with no logic change, confirmed by git diff and by the code-reviewer's own verification. Net effect on the threat model is positive, not neutral: the feature closes a gap where a stage could misreport a rename/deletion and have the claim-checker silently accept it as 'work not done' or silently miss a false deletion claim — it adds integrity checking, it does not remove any.
dependencyAudit: No new dependencies introduced — git diff of go.mod/go.sum against main is empty.
go mod verify: all modules verified.

stride.assessed: No identity or authentication surface exists in this code path — claims are self-reported by pipeline stages within the same trust level as before, and the orchestrator does not authenticate callers. Not applicable.

This is the category the feature strengthens. verifyDeletionClaim (internal/orchestrator/claims.go) checks a claimed deletion two ways: a filesystem stat (existingPaths, routed through the pre-existing resolveWithinRoot guard which rejects any path resolving outside the project root) and, when a WorkTree is configured, cross-checks against the git-observed changed set (unseenDeletions) so a path that was never actually touched cannot be claimed as deleted. requireNoRenameArrows closes the specific 'old -> new' single-field encoding that previously let a correct rename be misread. No new tampering surface was introduced; an existing gap was closed.

ClaimError names the stage, field, and paths, so a false or suspicious claim is attributable to the stage that made it, consistent with the existing MustExist claim errors. No audit trail was removed or weakened.

ClaimError messages and rendered markdown (render_implementation.go, render_qa.go) only echo repo-relative paths the agent itself supplied — no secrets, credentials, or user PII flow through this path. Rendering of FilesDeleted/TestFilesDeleted follows the exact same bullets()/frontmatter() pattern already used for FilesCreated/FilesModified, introducing no new sink.
(egress) No outbound network calls, API calls, or egress of any kind are introduced by this change — it is pure in-process filesystem stat and in-memory map lookup.

The new code paths (missingPaths/existingPaths/unseenDeletions) are the same O(n) loop-over-claimed-paths shape as the pre-existing MustExist checks, bounded by the same agent-report size as before — no new unbounded iteration or amplification was introduced.
No roles, permissions, or privilege levels are modeled or checked in this subsystem — not applicable.

securityChecklist.item: No hardcoded secrets, API keys, or credentials introduced
No new external dependency added (go.mod/go.sum unchanged)
Path handling for the new deletion-claim checks reuses the existing resolveWithinRoot project-root containment guard — no path traversal introduced
No new network, auth, session, or token handling introduced
Rendered output (markdown) uses the same bullet/frontmatter pattern as existing fields — no new injection sink
go vet and go mod verify clean; internal/state and internal/orchestrator test suites pass

notesForQa: No security-driven test additions were needed — this feature has no auth, network, or external-input trust boundary. The existing claims_test.go / implementation_chain_test.go / qa_state_test.go coverage (verified green in this review) already exercises the true-deletion, false-deletion, never-existed, and rename-arrow-rejection cases that map onto the TAMPERING assessment above.
